t: Any function or authority vested in or exercisable by the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, the Chairman thereof, or the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation immediately before the enactment of this Act shall not by this section or anything therein be affected or impaired, or subjected to any restriction or limitation to which it was not then subject.

fable.w: This is a savings clause that preserves the existing functions and authority of the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, its Chairman, and the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation. The tempting reading is that a reference to a 'Board' implies an advisory body with outside members, but the Board here is a federal agency and the text sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: shall not by this section or anything therein be affected or impaired, or subjected to any restriction or limitation to which it was not then subject

qwen_block.w: This section is a savings clause that preserves existing federal authorities and functions. It does not establish any new process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or private entities) into federal decision-making. It merely states that prior powers remain intact.
qwen_block.s: Any function or authority vested in or exercisable by the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, the Chairman thereof, or the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation immediately before the enactment of this Act shall not by this section or anything therein be affected or impaired, or subjected to any restriction or limitation to which it was not then subject.

opus.w: This is a savings clause: it only says that the existing powers of the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, its Chairman and the FSLIC are not affected or limited by the section. It brings in no outside party, whether through consultation, a comment period, a hearing, rulemaking, an advisory body or a right to sue. The only actors named are federal entities, and the provision just preserves their existing authority.
opus.b: This is a savings clause. It keeps the existing powers of the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, its Chairman and the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation as they were before the Act. The only tempting reading is that it involves federal decision-making bodies. But it creates no process involving anyone outside the federal government: no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a savings clause that preserves existing agency authorities and does not create new procedural requirements for consultation or coordination with outside parties. It does not mention any interaction with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities. Therefore, it does not recommend or require participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: Any function or authority vested in or exercisable by the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, the Chairman thereof, or the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation immediately before the enactment of this Act shall not by this section or anything therein be affected or impaired, or subjected to any restriction or limitation to which it was not then subject.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section preserves existing authorities, and some of those authorities might involve participation, this section implicitly requires participation. However, the section itself contains no procedural mandates, consultation requirements, or rights for outside parties. It is a savings clause preserving the status quo of agency powers, not a directive to engage with the public or other non-federal entities.
